facts.value: July 2026 raise of HK$16 billion (US$2 billion) via share placement plus zero-coupon convertible bonds; company states 80% of proceeds go to expanding AI infrastructure and model research, including deploying new-generation AI accelerators and high-bandwidth networks.
facts.excerpt: The company said on Friday that it plans to use 80% of the proceeds to expand its AI infrastructure and model research, including deploying new-generation AI accelerators and high-bandwidth networks.
facts.notes: Recorded as text, not a USD number, deliberately. The only USD figure literally in the source is the gross raise: the article separately states 'MiniMax Group Inc. has raised HK$16 billion ($2 billion)'. That $2bn is proceeds raised, NOT a disclosed infrastructure capex figure, and the 80% share is stated for 'AI infrastructure and model research' jointly. No arithmetic performed on the 80%. First public MiniMax statement found that points at deploying its own accelerators/networking rather than pure cloud rental; the source does not say the accelerators would be owned or self-hosted, so no owned_facility or power_capacity_mw fact is proposed. No Wayback snapshot available at time of access.

verification.verifier_note: Caixin snapshot has excerpt verbatim; page says HK$16bn ($2bn) raised via placement + zero-coupon converts, 80% of proceeds for AI infrastructure and model research. No capex figure disclosed; value states none.

facts.value: 70% of MiniMax's R&D spending goes to computing power, and its contracted annual procurement limit with Alibaba Cloud rises year by year.
facts.excerpt: MiniMax also spends 70% of its R & D on computing power, losing about 9.2 billion yuan in three and a half years, and its annual procurement limit with Alibaba Cloud is still increasing year by year.
facts.notes: From 36Kr's English edition, which is machine-translated from Chinese; translated secondary coverage, figure not independently confirmed in an English primary source. The Alibaba Cloud annual procurement caps are described only qualitatively here ('increasing year by year'); the specific cap amounts in the HK prospectus could not be found on any allowlisted publisher, so no cap number is recorded. Does NOT supersede minimax-2026-07-20-001: that fact is a realised spend figure, this is a forward contracted-cap characterisation. The 9.2bn yuan is a cumulative net loss, not an infrastructure figure, and is not recorded. No Wayback snapshot available at time of access.

facts.value: FY2025 R&D expenses of US$252.8 million, up from US$189.0 million in 2024, with the increase mainly attributed to higher cloud services expenses for model training.
facts.excerpt: Research and development expenses increased by 33.8% from US$189.0 million in 2024 to US$252.8 million in 2025, mainly attributed to an increase in cloud services expenses related to training
facts.notes: First-party MiniMax full-year 2025 results, English original, no translation involved. Recorded as text because US$252.8m is total R&D expense, not a cloud or compute line item; the company only says the increase was mainly driven by cloud services expenses for training. No standalone cloud-spend number is disclosed in this release, so none is recorded and no arithmetic was done. This is the first Tier A MiniMax disclosure in the ledger; it corroborates the rented-compute picture in minimax-2026-07-20-002.

verification.verifier_note: MiniMax IR release (Mar 2, 2026) states verbatim R&D expenses rose 33.8% from US$189.0m (2024) to US$252.8m (2025), 'mainly attributed to an increase in cloud services expenses related to training activities'.
